dod_intent_evidence: Own SBIR Phase II abstract: 'Powered Parafoil Vehicle Management System (PP-VMS) — Air Force 2022 ($849,807)' explicitly names Air Force PR and Special Operations Forces (SOF) as the mission customer and describes reducing combat risk to transport aircraft crews.
score_evidence: 'AGUV is simple, powerful, robust, low cost, and highly innovative' with zero mention of ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR anywhere on the site → deployment_awareness_absence (capped at 12: own-language word count ~964 < 1000)
SBIR awarded 2022, current employee count 2 ('Paragrine Systems, Llc employs 2 people (+100.0% YoY, +1 person)') with no visible Phase III transition news → stage_pressure
No jobs data in pack → hiring_profile_skew set to 10 baseline

blind_spots.blind_spot: PP-VMS's core value is JPADS-style 'waypoint following, loiter patterns, and autonomous path reversal' guidance, but the abstract never addresses GPS-denied or jammed navigation.
blind_spots.operator_reality: In a GPS-denied fight, the same waypoint/loiter guidance that makes PP-VMS valuable disappears exactly when SOF needs precision delivery most — there's no mention of INS backup, visual nav, or degraded-GPS fallback.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team appears to be aviation product-development generalists (per site bio) rather than avionics/GNC specialists focused on contested-environment navigation.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: mission programmability with waypoint following, loiter patterns, and autonomous path reversal

blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims 'reduced training requirements' for a brand-new vehicle management interface with no description of who trains aircrew or ground teams to actually use PP-VMS.
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Reduced training requirements' is asserted, not demonstrated — for SOF or PR teams under real time pressure, an unfamiliar VMS interface with no described training pipeline is exactly the kind of last-mile friction that keeps a proven prototype grounded.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The claim reads as a proposal-writing benefit statement rather than something validated with real operators.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: reduced training requirements and expanded mission capabilities

blind_spots.blind_spot: Proposes adapting the vehicle for 'weapons delivery' and SOF missions with zero mention of ITAR/export-control handling, from a company with only 2 employees.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A VMS proposed for weapons-delivery missions and SOF use is squarely inside ITAR territory; a 2-person shop with no visible compliance hire risks the same administrative freeze that stalls small defense primes before Phase III ever starts.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is technical/aviation-focused (per bio: 'hands-on business builders and technical visionaries with decades of experience in aviation product development'), not compliance-focused, and is too small to have a dedicated ITAR function.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: adapt powered parafoils for other missions such as ISR, weapons delivery, and decreasing pilot workload on manned operations

opener_hook: Paragrine Systems' 2022 Air Force Phase II SBIR ($849,807) proposes a parafoil vehicle-management system for SOF cargo and personnel delivery — the company is now down to 2 employees with no public sign of a Phase III transition.
what_they_do: Builds the AGUV, a powered-parafoil air/ground hybrid utility vehicle, and under an Air Force Phase II SBIR is developing a Powered Parafoil Vehicle Management System (PP-VMS) for SOF/PR cargo and personnel delivery.
